title: Slow-tier statistical escapability/fairness sweep for competitive mechanics (1000+ seeds)
description: Filed from TASK-058 review (rev-t058 L1). Each competitive mechanic's per-ticket escapability test uses ~20 seeds/pattern (a legitimate 'set de test' per GDD §4 for the mechanic ticket). GDD §ring-1 (line ~849) envisions a much larger 1000+ seed statistical sweep as a fairness gate. This ticket adds that broader sweep as a SLOW-tier / opt-in test run (kept out of the fast suite so it doesn't slow the TDD inner loop) covering the competitive mechanics as they land: MECH_02 ESQUIVA (TASK-058, done — escapability solver bot exists), and MECH_01 MANTÉN (TASK-060) + MECH_03 CORRE (TASK-059) + the asymmetric mechanics (TASK-040) as those close. Reuse each mechanic's existing solver/optimal-play oracle; assert the fairness property (optimal play survives / no forced loss) holds across the large seed set; surface any failing seed for design review. Gate it behind a slow-tier category/trait or a separate test project so CI's fast leg stays fast (coordinate with TASK-049's CI — the slow sweep could be a separate scheduled workflow, not per-push).
acceptance_criteria: A slow-tier statistical escapability sweep (1000+ seeds per pattern/mechanic) runs each competitive mechanic's optimal-play oracle and asserts the GDD fairness property across the set, kept OUT of the fast suite.
MECH_02 is covered first (its solver bot already exists); MECH_01/MECH_03/asymmetric mechanics are added as their tickets close, or a follow-up notes the deferral explicitly.
Any failing seed is surfaced (logged, not silently skipped) for design review rather than auto-passing.
The sweep is invokable on demand and/or via a scheduled CI workflow separate from the per-push fast leg (coordinate with TASK-049).
